question: At unaccepted cold q, which relative joint/face/shaft/panel motions limit the reference-linear contact and own-seat applicability?
method: Read only authenticated diagnostic_last_q, reference timber map and source geometry. Verify three raw/canonical/q/state identities against the existing ledger; all fields retain converged=false, usable actions=false and no response.q.

Reconstruct original fitting/panel/shaft indices from frozen production ordering and pure geometry events; exact20/36/6/70 body and8018 coordinate census is mandatory. No K is read, assembled or solved.

Reuse reviewed point_displacement for each linear timber point and current_pose_from_map for finite rigid-arm/geodesic mechanical point/director replay. Append70 zero first-twist gauges only in a pose facade; these are not new response coordinates, torque restraints or accepted finite-shaft gauges.

Retain signed relative point motions and relative material rotations, separating fitting beam-vs-post pose deformation from joint body rotations. Shaft-axis director tilt is the gauge-independent shaft/host comparison; full shaft material-roll comparison remains gauge-dependent.

Finite panel points and surface normals come from the existing saved Ritz surface helper. A rigid panel rotation or finite material in-plane frame is not assigned; only local panel/receiver normal tilt is compared.

For normal contacts positive projection is opening. Compare reference-linear signed motion to exact-arm motion under fixed source normals and updated second-body material normals. Fixed-q side changes are unsolved applicability markers, never modified contact forces or admitted branches.

For each own capture compare its actual pressure/support datums, shaft-axis/host-face relative tilt and finite/linear normal/tangential compatibility. The frozen model provides point-only axial capture with no annular pressure couple, preload or friction.

Evaluate all272 cells in six source timber overlap patches; compare local tangential motion to25-mm cell width and recorded tangential bounding extents. Source overlap geometry is retained, but current trimmed footprint overlap/pressure is not computed.
limits: Every cold q remains unaccepted and its floor mask is inconsistent. Reported motions are diagnostic numerical markers, not physical deflections, contact forces, strength or global stability.

Exact finite rigid-arm rotation at fixed diagnostic q is a kinematic applicability comparison. It does not update equilibrium, load locations, beam constitutive law, contact activation or candidate demands.

Geodesic interpolation of donor nodal rotations and straight centerline interpolation does not prove a curved timber/shaft solution or mesh refinement. Formed heel radius/hole effects remain unqualified; sharp modeled B104 solids are ideal geometry.
The fitting beam-vs-post rotation/translation is a two-port heel-flexibility marker, not local formed-metal heel curvature or resistance.

Washer body rotation, seating contact area, annular pressure moments, delivered tolerances and joint preload are absent from the point-only end-capture model. Tilt/offset/occupied-diameter comparisons do not supply them.

Timber contact cell drift and changing own normals can invalidate fixed-cell correspondence even where local rotations are modest. Bounding extents are descriptive scales; no lost overlap or new deformation limit is inferred. Actual deformed trimmed-face projection, bore voids and contact area require a separate verified geometric/contact method.
No stiffness matrix, CAD rebuild, native solve, global solve, external/old force transfer, fabrication, redesign, capacity assignment or release occurs.
